channel.title: AI Agents on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in AI Agents on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: ai: Build trusted autonomous agents for your team with Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry announces guidance for building trusted autonomous agents for teams, framing the problem as trust and governance rather than raw agent capability.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: What’s new in Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft announces Ignite 2026 updates for Foundry Agent Service, focused on making agents more reliable in production by improving context handling, tool use, runtime resilience, and iterative improvement.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Agent Grid helping secure AI agent communications
item.description:
Agent Grid is now in public preview for supported Azure environments. It adds identity-based Zero Trust network security so security teams can centrally govern communication between agents, models, tools, and external services.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Agent Sandbox cluster extension
item.description:
Azure is introducing a public preview of an Agent Sandbox cluster extension for Kubernetes. It provides isolated environments for AI agent sessions that run untrusted, model-generated code, reducing the need for teams to build their own sandbox lifecycle and related operational logic.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Bring-your-own image and Cosmos DB MCP server in Azure Connector Namespace hosted MCP​
item.description:
Azure Connector Namespace now offers a public preview of hosted MCP server capability, letting AI agents use tools without developers managing a separate hosting stack. The preview also adds support for bring-your-own image and a Cosmos DB MCP server.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Managed MCP Server in Azure Cosmos DB
item.description:
Azure Cosmos DB now has a public preview of a managed, hosted MCP server for connecting enterprise AI agents to business data through a standard MCP endpoint. The preview supports schema discovery, document retrieval, and full-text/vector search.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Connector Namespace
item.description:
Azure Connector Namespace is now generally available. It provides a fully managed integration service for connecting applications and AI agents to Microsoft, SaaS, and enterprise systems through prebuilt, reusable connectors.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB Shell
item.description:
Azure Cosmos DB Shell is now generally available. It provides a command-line, scriptable workflow for working with Azure Cosmos DB, including support for AI agents.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management and Azure AI Gateway
item.description:
Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management and Azure AI Gateway is now generally available. It lets organizations centrally govern AI agents and MCP tools and enforce security and access policies at runtime.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure MCP Server 3.0
item.description:
Azure MCP Server 3.0 is now generally available. The release expands Azure integration for AI agents and developer tools via the open Model Context Protocol (MCP), including new infrastructure-as-code support through Azure Terraform.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Agents are your newest insiders. Security must move at their speed.
item.description:
Microsoft announced new capabilities in Microsoft 365 E7 and Project Perception aimed at helping organizations contain AI agent risk and continuously adapt protection. The post frames agents as insider-like risks and focuses on security controls that keep pace with their behavior.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: Copilot to autopilot: Why no single safeguard is enough
item.description:
Microsoft says it built a layered control model for an AI agent to handle production network incidents autonomously, but only within defined identity, authorization, tooling, and human-approval boundaries. The article argues that no single safeguard is sufficient for production use.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: dotnet: Durable Task in the Real World: What Problems Does It Actually Solve?
item.description:
The post outlines practical cases where durable execution is useful, where it is unnecessary, and how it relates to AI agents. It frames Durable Task as a tool for workflows that need reliable state, retries, and long-running coordination.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Microsoft SQL Agent Skills
item.description:
Microsoft SQL Agent Skills are in public preview. They provide product-specific guidance for AI agents used to build, operate, and migrate SQL workloads across Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Database container, and SQL Server migration scenarios.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: ​​​​​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: September 2026​​
item.description:
Microsoft Security’s September 2026 update focuses on discovering and controlling local AI agents, extending Zero Trust controls to agent traffic, and improving SOC foundational capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Foundry Routines in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Foundry Agent Service now includes Foundry Routines in public preview. This adds a native trigger primitive so published agents can run automatically on schedules or in response to business events.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Build Your Own AI Agent Harness in C#, the MafClaw Live Series
item.description:
Microsoft is running a 4-part live series showing how to build a C# AI agent harness with Microsoft Agent Framework, starting from a single IChatClient call and evolving it into a production-ready agent with observability and governance. The post is an announcement for the series and does not include technical implementation details.

  • Source: .NET
